cells.tense: You are in the middle of shared work and what came of it is showing now, where both of you can see.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Start the piece of shared work you two keep circling, this week, badly if that is how it starts, and stay in it long enough to learn what actually holds between you.
cells.core:
What you tended is coming up. In the middle of what you and another person are building, the work is showing what it was for — something both of you can stand inside and see, and you are awake enough to notice it is not finished. This is what patience built, and it is still being built.

The hard part is the last one. You can stay with what you share past the pleasant, uncomplicated stretch into the piece that tests it, and nothing in you needs the friction to be a verdict on anything. Bring that to the work you two are making: start the part you keep putting off, and stay long enough to see what holds. Whatever you find beats the guessing — and the commitment is yours to keep or set down, not something this has settled.
cells.sheetLine: What you tended is ripe. Eat it where both can see.
cells.verb: tending something until it comes up abundant
cells.place: in the live middle of what you and another are making together

cells.tense: You are already living in the result that hasn't come up yet, and building the room to store it in.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring one piece of the work you have been carrying alone and do it alongside them, nothing prepared, letting the piece take the shape two people give it.
cells.core:
The harvest is in your head and the fields are still green. In what you and another person are building, you are already living in the season after this one — the outcome, the expanded version, what you want it to become — and you have been pulling it forward by holding it. The other person stands in the actual work, and from there it reads as being planned at, not built with. Care that runs ahead leaves them holding slack.

Nothing calms that, so this: take one piece of work you have been doing on your own and do it next to them, nothing prepared. Their pace is honest about where the river actually runs, and that is where you can flow with it instead of above it.

cells.tense: You have stood outside the shared work long enough that it went quiet, and that door is behind you now.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Make one honest move toward someone you actually want closer — a call, a plan — and take the second step before you know how the first landed.
cells.core:
What you and another person were building has gone quiet, and you are on the far side of a door that already closed. The abundance isn't gone — it is unspent. It waits in the middle of nothing, and something in you decided that walking back in is a risk worth avoiding. From there, every meeting looks decided before it starts, and the thinking about it runs all day while nothing is being kept.

Don't force feeling back into the quiet place. Charge the other thing instead: choose somebody you want closer and make one honest move — a call, a question, a plan. Then take a second step before you know how the first one landed. The warmth arrives after the foot moves, not before.

cells.tense: You keep showing up for what you share and describe it as just how things happened to go.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Give the piece of your shared life that costs you most a fixed hour in your own week, alone, not folded in with everything else. Show up for that hour once, even badly.
cells.core:
This did not simply unfold and carry you along. What you and another person have was tended — by you — and you speak about the hours and the patience as things that happened rather than things you did. You would have to be caught giving them to admit it, so nobody has caught you. The pen sits pointing the other way.

Do one hard thing where you can watch yourself do it: name the piece of this that costs the most and give it a fixed hour in your own week, alone, not folded in with everything else. Then show up for the hour once. What you keep will match what you put in, and the page can carry your name.
cells.sheetLine: You keep showing up for it and count it as circumstance.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I'd flag first: the Too Little core says the shared thing 'went quiet' — the record gives the Flourishing signature as a transient about abundance and the seat as connection, and the person will know exactly which door closed, so this leans on biography the record doesn't hold; narrowed to what's visible in how they meet what touches them now, it stands. The reader's likely objection across all four is 'you're naming what's underneath' — the Unacknowledged cell, in particular, tells them they're authoring and calling it circumstance; if that's wrong they can still say so and use the ask, which only asks for one kept hour in their own week. The ask survives an error in every cell, because each is done alone by the person, needs no witness, and proves nothing about the reading. One sentence serves me more than them and should come out: any version of 'what you keep is the work' that lands as praise for what the reader invented.

attempts.check: The gateway's flags are answered in the rewrite: the Too Little core now stays with what the person can see in front of them and does not narrate what happened at the door, so a reader can say 'no, that isn't it' and still use the ask. The quartet's asks are rebuilt on four different opening verbs — start, bring, make, give — and only one carries a clock, so a person who draws twice does not meet the same instruction. The four faces read as opposite failures of one capacity: running ahead of the shared work, drained out of it, and disowning authorship of it. One sentence serves me more than the reader and should come out: any version of 'what you keep is the work' delivered as a tribute nobody asked for.
